sentences.text: Phosphatosaurus was a large dyrosaurid, a group of crocodylomorphs, possessing a skull longer than one meter and blunt teeth.
The tip of its snout was spoon-shaped because the rostral part of the lower jaw expanded laterally.
Its mouth featured nonhomodont dentition with unique paired tooth sockets in the lower jaw that sat closer together than adjacent ones.
The close relationship between Phosphatosaurus and the Cretaceous genus Sokotosuchus implies a long ghost lineage extending back to the Maastrichtian that lacks fossil evidence.
The genus was named in 1955 and remains monotypic, containing only the type species P. gavialoides.
Researchers suggest that the gaps between the paired tooth sockets in the lower jaw may have accommodated larger upper teeth.
Phosphatosaurus is classified as a basal dyrosaurid and is frequently placed near the base of dyrosaurid phylogenetic trees.
Most phylogenetic analyses show Phosphatosaurus and Sokotosuchus forming a clade that is more closely related to each other than to any other dyrosaurid genus.
Eric Buffetaut assigned Phosphatosaurus to the subfamily Phosphatosaurinae in 1979, defining it as a clade with Sokotosaurus.
Fossils have been found in Tunisia and Mali.
The time range for Phosphatosaurus spans from the Campanian to the Ypresian, approximately 83.6 to 48.07 million years ago.
Recent studies have tentatively questioned the validity of the Phosphatosaurinae subfamily due to limited anatomical knowledge of the genera involved.
